question.text: A monoatomic gas of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn><mo> </mo><mi>u</mi></math> is kept in an insulated container. The container is moving with velocity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>30</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. If the container is suddenly stopped then a change in temperature of the gas (<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo></math>gas constant) is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>R</mi></mrow></mfrac></math>. Value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is,

solution.text:
Given that mass of gas is 4u hence its molar mass M is 4 g mol-1

∴12mv2=nCvΔT

⇒12 m×302=mM×3R2×ΔT

∴  ΔT=36003R
